text:
ConocoPhillips edged up 0.28% today, a modest gain that reflects the broader steadiness in oil markets—US crude is holding near $89.50 a barrel and global oil near $93, prices that have been relatively stable over the past week despite the stock's 2% dip since mid-November. The company recovered from Friday's sharp drop (when the stock fell nearly 3% to $132.19) but remains below the levels it hit earlier in the week, suggesting lingering caution among investors.

The collapse of fossil fuel commitments at the U.N. climate summit (COP31) over the weekend may have provided some relief to energy stocks—the rejection of a deal that would have included language on phasing down oil and gas lifted concerns that stricter climate mandates were imminent. That said, the modest size of today's gain and the stock's overall two-week weakness suggest that headline risk and uncertainty around energy policy are keeping investors from fully committing to the sector.
